findings.text: Independent Opus review returned pass_with_notes, 0 blocking: all 5 ACs met, classify never misreports a stale run as blocked (terminal and explicit-blocker precedence verified, strict-> boundary at 30s), both events.py and both capabilities.yaml copies byte-identical, the five run.* milestones in the committed vocabulary while run.step/run.heartbeat are live-only, run folder under .git (outside history), stdlib and ASCII, no protected path. The classify stale mutation was caught by two selftest assertions (778/2).

Two review notes closed PRE-SHIP with non-tautological selftest teeth, self-verified by direct evaluation: an absent heartbeat now classifies stale not active (matching the spec Notes), and read_live now skips a torn/partial trailing line instead of crashing; removing either guard changes the value its assertion checks.

Remaining non-blocking follow-ups (filed, not fixed here): the atomic temp-plus-rename mechanism has no dedicated race test; meta.json write-once is a caller convention; _next_seq is O(n^2) over a very long live log and will become a cached counter when the executor owns the run in R2.

summary: WARP-0501 (R1 of PLAN-0005, the Run Lens run registry) is correct and honest. Independent adversarial review pass_with_notes, 0 blocking; gate GREEN (selftest 783). The registry stores a run's live state in a per-run folder under the git common dir (outside git history), writes state atomically, appends sequenced live progress, and classifies active/blocked/stale/done with the load-bearing rule that a stale heartbeat is never reported as blocked. Five durable run milestones entered the committed vocabulary while high-volume progress stays live-only; both events.py and both capabilities.yaml copies are byte-identical. Two review notes were closed pre-ship with non-tautological teeth; proof_digest recomputed via validate.py.
